mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY > 5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points month-over-month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE MoM > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a contraction in economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 QoQ < -1% does not correlate with subsequent economic contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% year-over-year signals robust economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, the combination signals aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of FEDFUNDS > 5% and rising CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 month-over-month signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or PAYEMS MoM < -100,000 does not correlate with subsequent labor market weakness.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% year-over-year signals robust demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST YoY > 10% does not correlate with subsequent housing market strength.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the real GDP (GDPC1) is growing, the combination signals accommodative monetary policy supporting economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of FEDFUNDS < 1% and GDPC1 QoQ > 0 does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.
